name: Prepositions
moduleIntroduction:
Welcome to the Prepositions module! Prepositions are small words like 'in', 'on', 'at', 'for', and 'to' that show time, place, or direction. 

Why is this difficult? Because there is often no logic! For example, we say 'on the bus' but 'in the car'. Also, French speakers often translate directly from 'à', 'de', or 'en', which leads to errors. For example, French says 'marié avec' (with), but English says 'married to'. In this module, we will learn the rules for Time and Place, and memorize the tricky verbs that always take specific prepositions.
contrastiveExplanation:
Here are the main differences between French and English prepositions:

AT / ON / IN (Time):
• AT + Exact Time: at 8pm, at noon.
• ON + Day/Date: on Monday, on my birthday.
• IN + Month/Year/Season: in May, in 2024, in summer.

AT / ON / IN (Place):
• IN + Enclosed Space/City/Country: in the room, in Douala, in Cameroon.
• ON + Surface: on the table, on the wall.
• AT + Point/Location: at the bus stop, at home, at work.

Direct Translation Errors:
• 'Discuss about': In French 'discuter de'. In English, 'discuss' takes NO preposition. (Discuss the problem).
• 'Married with': In French 'marié avec'. In English, 'Married TO'.
• 'Good in': In French 'bon en'. In English, 'Good AT'.
• 'Arrive at/in': Use 'arrive IN' for cities/countries, 'arrive AT' for buildings/stations. Never 'arrive to'.

commonErrors.wrong: She is married with a doctor.
commonErrors.correct: She is married to a doctor.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Direct translation of 'marié avec'. In English, you are married TO someone.
French uses 'discuter de'. English 'discuss' is transitive (no preposition).
French uses 'à' for both position and movement. English uses 'to' for movement (go to) and 'at' for position (stay at).
French uses 'bon en'. English uses 'good at'.
Confusion between specific dates (on) and long periods like years (in).

items.feedback: Correct! We use 'at' for specific clock times.
Correct! We use 'on' for days of the week.
Correct! We use 'in' for months, years, and seasons.
Correct! We use 'in' for cities, countries, and towns.
Correct! We use 'on' for surfaces.
Correct! We use 'to' for movement or direction (go to, come to).

items.questionText: He is waiting ___ the bus stop.
items.feedback: Correct! We use 'at' for a specific point or location.
Correct! We always say 'look at' something.
Correct! We use 'in' for enclosed spaces (inside).

items.questionText: I will see you ___ the afternoon.
items.feedback: Correct! We say 'in the morning', 'in the afternoon', 'in the evening'.
Correct! We use 'in' for continents and countries.
Correct! We always say 'listen to'.
Correct! 'Under' means below or beneath something.
Correct! We use 'in' for years.
Correct! We say 'talk to' (or 'speak to') someone.
Correct! 'At' is used for specific times.

items.questionText: There is a picture ___ the wall.
items.feedback: Correct! A wall is a surface, so we use 'on'.
Correct! We always say 'wait for' someone/something.
Correct! 'Next to' means beside.

items.questionText: We don't go to school ___ Sundays.
items.feedback: Correct! We use 'on' for days of the week.
Correct! With skills, we use 'good at' or 'bad at'. (Not 'in').
Correct! We always say 'interested in'.
Correct! In English, you are married 'to' someone (not 'with').

items.questionText: I usually go to work ___ bus.
items.feedback: Correct! We use 'by' for general modes of transport (by bus, by car, by plane).

items.questionText: But today, I am ___ the bus now.
items.feedback: Correct! When you are inside a large vehicle (bus, train, plane) where you can stand up, we use 'on'.
Correct! We say 'at work', 'at home', 'at school' (as a general location).
Correct! We always say 'afraid of' (or scared of).
Correct! We always say 'depend on'.
Correct! We say 'arrive in' a city or country.

items.questionText: When did you arrive ___ the airport?
items.feedback: Correct! We say 'arrive at' a building, station, or specific place.
Correct! 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.
Correct! We always say 'belong to'.
Correct! You agree 'with' a person.

items.questionText: My car is parked ___ the bank and the post office.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Between' is used for two things.

items.questionText: I didn't watch the match. I was ___ holiday.
items.feedback: Correct! We say 'on holiday', 'on vacation', 'on a trip'.

items.questionText: Please take your feet ___ the table!
items.feedback: Correct! 'Off' means 'away from a surface'. It is the opposite of 'on'.

items.questionText: Cameroon is famous ___ its football team.
items.feedback: Correct! We always say 'famous for' something.
Correct! We say 'worried about' something.
Correct! We say 'by credit card' or 'by check', BUT 'in cash'.
Correct! We say 'laugh at' someone.

items.questionText: Find the error: "We need to discuss about the project."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Discuss' is a transitive verb. It does NOT take a preposition. Say 'Discuss the project'.

items.questionText: The train leaves in 5 minutes. We are just ___ time.
items.feedback: Correct! 'In time' means 'early enough' (before it's too late). 'On time' means 'at the scheduled time'.

items.questionText: Find the error: "I entered into the room."
items.feedback: Correct! When entering a physical place, we use 'enter' without a preposition. 'Enter into' is used for agreements/contracts.

items.questionText: He was accused ___ stealing the money.
items.feedback: Correct! The verb pattern is 'accuse someone OF doing something'.

items.questionText: The rain prevented us ___ playing football.
items.feedback: Correct! The pattern is 'prevent someone FROM doing something'.
Correct! 'Through' is used for 3D spaces (forests, tunnels, crowds). 'Across' is for flat surfaces.
Correct! We use 'made OF' when the material doesn't change form (you can still see the wood). We use 'made FROM' when the material changes (Paper is made from wood).

items.questionText: I dream ___ becoming a doctor one day.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Dream OF' usually means an ambition or deep desire. 'Dream ABOUT' usually refers to dreams while sleeping.

items.questionText: I object ___ being treated like this!
items.feedback: Correct! The pattern is 'object TO doing something'. 'To' is a preposition here, so it is followed by the gerund (-ing).

items.questionText: ___ the end, we decided to stay home.
items.feedback: Correct! 'In the end' means 'finally' or 'after a long time'. 'At the end' refers to a specific point (At the end of the book).
items.subTopic: In the end vs At the end

items.feedback: Correct! We say 'suffer FROM' a disease.
Correct! 'Refrain FROM' means to stop yourself from doing something.

items.questionText: She is not capable ___ doing the job.
items.feedback: Correct! We say 'capable OF' (adjective + preposition). But we say 'able TO' (adjective + infinitive).

items.questionText: He threw the ball ___ me (to catch it).
items.feedback: Correct! You throw 'TO' someone if you want them to catch it. You throw 'AT' someone if you want to hit/hurt them.

items.questionText: This song reminds me ___ my childhood.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Remind of' means something makes you remember the past. 'Remind about' means to tell someone not to forget a task.
Correct! We say 'congratulate someone ON' something.
Correct! You are angry WITH a person, but angry ABOUT a situation.

items.questionText: The manager is responsible ___ the staff.
items.feedback: Correct! You are 'responsible FOR' something/someone.
Correct! 'Believe IN' means to believe something exists or is good. 'Believe' (no preposition) means to think something is true.
Correct! 'By mistake' is a fixed expression. Similarly: 'By accident'.

Correct! We say 'arrive in' a country.
Correct! We say 'arrive at' a specific point or building (station).

Correct! We always say 'belong to'.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Between' is used for two people.

items.feedback: Correct! We say 'on business' (work trip).

items.questionText: Don't worry ___ the money. I will pay.

items.questionText: The bus is always ___ time. It never arrives late.
items.feedback: Correct! 'On time' means 'at the scheduled time'.

items.questionText: Find the error: "She entered into the bank."
items.feedback: Correct! Use 'enter' (no preposition) for entering a place.

items.questionText: You cannot accuse him ___ being lazy.

items.feedback: Correct! The pattern is 'prevent someone FROM doing something'.

items.questionText: ___ the end of the film, everyone was crying.

items.feedback: Correct! We say 'suffer FROM' a condition.

items.questionText: He threw a stone ___ the angry dog.
items.feedback: Correct! You throw 'AT' something when you want to hit it (aggression).

items.questionText: Please remind me ___ call my mother.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Remind TO' means do not forget an action. 'Remind OF' is about memory.

items.questionText: I congratulated him ___ passing his exam.
items.feedback: Correct! We say 'congratulate someone ON' something.

items.questionText: The students are angry ___ the new rules.
items.feedback: Correct! You are angry ABOUT a situation/thing, but angry WITH a person.
Correct! You are 'responsible FOR' something.

items.questionText: If you don't believe ___ yourself, nobody will.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Believe IN' means to have confidence/trust in.

items.questionText: We met ___ accident at the market.
items.feedback: Correct! 'By accident' is a fixed expression. It means 'not planned'.
